content:
To merge the last two commits into one, use an interactive rebase:

```bash
git rebase -i HEAD~2
```

An editor will open showing something like:

```text
pick abc1234 First commit message
pick def5678 Second commit message
```

Change the second `pick` to `squash` (or `s`):

```text
pick abc1234 First commit message
squash def5678 Second commit message
```

Save and close the editor.

Then Git will let you edit the combined commit message. Save that too.

### If you've already pushed
If those commits were pushed to a remote, you'll need to force-push after rebasing:

```bash
git push --force-with-lease
```

### Quick alternative
If you just want to combine the last commit into the previous one and keep the previous message:

```bash
git reset --soft HEAD~1
git commit --amend
```

If you want, I can also show the safest way depending on whether the commits were already pushed.
